detail.longDescription: Finally published my new blog post: GitLab, OpenTofu, HCL… and Nix ! How do you manage 250+ GitLab repositories, 230+ users, and dozens of configuration policies without drowning in ClickOps ? Well, what if you could manage all of that declaratively, using Nix and OpenTofu ? The interesting part: instead of writing HCL directly, we use Terranix and the Nix module system to generate OpenTofu configurations. This gives us powerful configuration composition, reusable abstractions, semantic merging, conflict detection, and reproducibility... while OpenTofu handles the actual resource lifecycle. The result ? GitLab configuration managed as code, with version control, merge requests, automated plans, and drift detection. In this new article, I explain the architecture, the challenges we encountered, and why I believe Nix and OpenTofu are a match made in heaven. ⚠️ Warning: Contains quite a bit of Nix, some HCL, and a healthy dose of memes and links, perhaps a bit too much... anyway, you have been warned.
